title: Orchestrate artifact rotation and rollback safeguards for profile release
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Our current CI/CD flow for model onboarding builds artifacts, produces a signed performance profile, and promotes the profile to the public catalog. We lack a coordinated artifact-rotation policy and robust, automated rollback mechanisms when a newly-published profile causes regressions (quality/latency/cost) in serving. This ticket implements an orchestration layer that ensures safe rotation of signed artifacts, atomic promotion/pinning semantics, automatic canary evaluation gating, and a fast, auditable rollback path.

Goals: 1) Ensure every published profile is cryptographically signed and versioned with immutable provenance metadata. 2) Implement atomic promotion and pinning semantics so consumers see a single consistent profile state. 3) Add automatic canary evaluation post-promotion with configurable thresholds that trigger automated rollback and alerting. 4) Provide an artifact-rotation policy to retire old artifacts safely and support key rotation without breaking pinned deployments. 5) Add audit/logging traces and a small operator CLI for emergency retraction with one-click re-pinning to the previous stable profile.

Acceptance criteria: - CI pipeline builds, signs, and uploads artifacts with provenance info (build metadata, git sha, profile hash) to the model registry. - Promotion step supports an atomic pin operation: either the new profile is promoted or the previous pin remains. - Canary jobs run automatically after promotion (10% traffic to new profile) and emit pass/fail signals to release controller. - If canary fails thresholds (quality drop >2% or latency increase >15%), pipeline performs automated rollback and posts incident to #runtime-incidents. - All promotion/rollback operations are recorded in the audit log with operator identity and KMS key ID. - Operators can perform manual rollback via Redwood CLI (redwoodctl profile rollback --to <profile>) which triggers edge broadcast and registry pin update. - Integration tests exist in CI that simulate a failing profile and verify automated rollback path.

Technical approach: - Extend the current publish-service (publishd) with a promotion controller that implements optimistic locking and a two-phase publish/pin commit. Use the artifact store (s3-like) object metadata to store signed manifests. - Add a lightweight state machine: BUILD -> SIGNED -> PUBLISHED (canary) -> PINNED. Only a successful canary transitions PUBLISHED -> PINNED; failures cause RETRACT -> revert pin. - Implement canary evaluation harness using the existing perf-eval job runner; add new metrics exporter that writes canary results to metrics-store and the release controller subscribes. - Store rotation policy in registry as JSON blob with TTLs; implement garbage-collector job that safely deletes unpinned artifacts older than retention window. - Support KMS key rotation by including key history in signed manifest and storing per-artifact key-id in registry. Include verification logic that accepts signatures from previous key ids for a configurable grace period.

Rollout plan: - Week 1: Add promotion controller and two-phase commit in a staged feature branch; add unit tests. - Week 2: Wire canary evaluation and metrics export; add integration test that performs synthetic canary. - Week 3: Add rollback CLI, audit logging, and GC policy; deploy to staging and run model-onboard canaries for 3 models. - Week 4: Gradual rollout to prod with 2-week monitoring window and manual approval gates at each step.

Monitoring & dashboards: - New dashboard: "Profile Promotions" showing promotion latency, canary pass rate, rollback occurrences, and per-model quality deltas. - Alert: canary-failure-high (triggered on >1 automatic rollback within 24h for same model) posts to #runtime-incidents and pings on-call. - SLO: maximal time-to-rollback after failure <= 5 minutes for automated rollbacks.

Testing: - Add CI integration test suite that simulates a profile with degraded quality (using evaluation harness) and asserts rollback occurs and registry pin restored. - Add fuzz tests for manifest signature verification including old-key grace period.

Risks & mitigations: - Risk: false positive canary triggers noisy rollbacks. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds, require two consecutive failing canaries OR alert with manual override. - Risk: GC deletes an artifact still referenced by a pinned deployment. Mitigation: GC only deletes unpinned artifacts older than retention window; double-check registry pins before deletion.

Artifacts & links: - Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/infra/Artifact+Rotation+and+Rollback+Design - RFC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/82 - Staging runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4d - Perf dashboard (staging): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ABCD/profile-promotions-staging

2025-02-24: Prototype promotion-controller branch created (github.com/redwood-inference/publishd/tree/feature/promotion-controller). Basic optimistic-locking implemented.
2025-02-27: Security review notes: require signed manifests to include key-id and key-rotation policy. Security to sign-off after adding key history. Action: Asha to update manifest schema.
